# API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_api_reference.py from the running server. Do not edit by hand. -->

The tools, resources and errors of Laravel MCP Companion 0.15, as a client sees them with
`--transform-mode none`. In the default `search` mode the same tools are reached through the
`search_tools` and `call_tool` meta-tools, which belong to FastMCP and are not described here.

[VERSIONING.md](VERSIONING.md) says which parts of this are covered by the compatibility promise.
`tests/protocol/contract.json` is the machine-readable form of the same surface.

## Results

Every tool returns two things: text for a model to read, and `structuredContent`, an object that
satisfies the tool's output schema. The text is the same object encoded as
[TOON](https://toonformat.dev), except for the two read tools, whose text is the page's markdown.

A field marked *always* is present in every successful result. Other fields are present when they
apply.

## Errors

A tool that cannot do what was asked returns a result with `isError: true` and this object as its
structured content (and, TOON-encoded, as its text):

```json
{"error": {"code": "unknown_version", "message": "Laravel version '99.x' is not available", "details": {"supported_versions": ["12.x", "13.x"]}}}
```

`code` is what to branch on. `message` is for a person or a model. `details` is present when there
is something that helps the caller recover.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `invalid_argument` | An argument was missing, empty or not one of the allowed values. |
| `unknown_version` | A Laravel version this server does not carry. |
| `not_found` | The named file, section, package, service, category or path does not exist. |
| `access_denied` | A path that resolves outside the documentation tree. |
| `update_failed` | A documentation update could not be completed. |
| `internal` | Anything unexpected. The message says which tool failed. |

Finding nothing is not an error: a search with no hits succeeds with `count: 0`.

An argument the framework itself rejects, such as one the tool does not have, produces FastMCP's
own validation error, which is text only.

## Documentation

### `search_laravel_docs`

Search Laravel's documentation and get back the sections that answer the question.

Covers every corpus on this server at once: the framework docs for the selected Laravel version, the first-party services (Forge, Vapor, Envoyer, Nova, Cloud, Nightwatch, Herd), fetched package docs (Livewire, Filament, Inertia, Spatie and others) and learning resources. Each result names a file and a section; pass both to read_laravel_doc_section to read just that section.

Use it first for any Laravel question. Narrow with `sources` when you know the corpus, and set `version` for an older Laravel release. Results are ranked across corpora, and no single source takes the whole page when others match. Nothing found is a normal result with count 0.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `query` | string | required | What to look for, as a question or as keywords |  |
| `version` | string | `null` | Laravel version for the framework docs (e.g. "12.x"). Defaults to the server's configured version. Services, packages and learning resources are not Laravel-versioned. |  |
| `all_versions` | boolean | `false` | Search every Laravel version instead of one |  |
| `sources` | array of string | `null` | Restrict the search to any of "core", "services", "packages", "learning". Default: all four | `core`, `services`, `packages`, `learning` |
| `limit` | integer | `5` | How many results to return, 1 to 20. Default 5 | 1 to 20 |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `query` | string | yes |  |
| `scope` | string | yes | The Laravel versions searched, comma-separated |
| `sources` | array of string | yes | One of `core`, `services`, `packages`, `learning`. |
| `count` | integer | yes | How many results follow; 0 when nothing matched |
| `matched_needs` | array of string |  | Common tasks recognised in the query, whose usual documentation pages were favoured |
| `results` | array of object | yes |  |
| `results[].file` | string | yes | Pass to read_laravel_doc_section or read_laravel_doc_content |
| `results[].section` | string | yes | Pass to read_laravel_doc_section with `file` |
| `results[].heading` | string | yes |  |
| `results[].score` | number | yes |  |
| `results[].snippet` | string | yes |  |
| `results[].source` | string | yes | core, service:<name>, package:<name> or learning:<name> |

### `read_laravel_doc_section`

Read one section of a documentation page.

Give it the `file` and `section` of a search result and it returns that section's markdown and nothing else. This is the cheap way to read: a whole page such as queues.md runs to tens of thousands of tokens, and an answer usually needs one section of it.

`section` may be an anchor ("dealing-with-failed-jobs"), a heading ("Dealing With Failed Jobs") or a heading written as a slug. If the section is not found, the error lists the sections the page does have.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `filename` | string | required | The page, as search returns it: "queues.md", "12.x/queues.md" or "forge/servers/php.md" |  |
| `section` | string | required | The section's anchor or heading, as search returns it |  |
| `version` | string | `null` | Laravel version for a framework page named without one. Ignored for service, package and learning pages |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `file` | string | yes |  |
| `version` | string |  | Laravel version, for a framework page |
| `corpus` | string |  | The service, package or learning source, for any other page |
| `section` | string | yes |  |
| `heading` | string | yes |  |
| `content` | string | yes | The section as markdown; the same text as the result's text content |

### `read_laravel_doc_content`

Read a whole documentation page, or just its outline.

mode="outline" returns the page's headings, which is the way to see what a page covers before reading any of it. mode="full" returns the entire page as markdown. Full pages are large; when you want one topic, search and read_laravel_doc_section cost a fraction of the tokens.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `filename` | string | required | The page: "queues.md", "12.x/queues.md" or "forge/servers/php.md" |  |
| `version` | string | `null` | Laravel version for a framework page named without one |  |
| `mode` | string | `"full"` | "full" for the whole page, "outline" for its headings only | `full`, `outline` |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `file` | string | yes |  |
| `version` | string |  | Laravel version, for a framework page |
| `corpus` | string |  | The service, package or learning source, for any other page |
| `mode` | string | yes | One of `full`, `outline`. |
| `content` | string |  | mode=full: the whole page as markdown |
| `headings` | array of object |  | mode=outline: every heading in order |
| `headings[].level` | integer | yes |  |
| `headings[].text` | string | yes |  |
| `headings[].section` | string | yes | For a level-2 heading, what to pass to read_laravel_doc_section; empty otherwise |

### `list_laravel_docs`

List what documentation this server holds.

With no arguments: every collection (each Laravel version, service, package and learning source) with its page count. With `source`, only that kind. With `name` (a Laravel version such as "12.x", or a service or package such as "forge"), that collection's files, named the way the read tools accept them.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `source` | string | `null` | Only this kind of collection: "core", "services", "packages" or "learning" | `core`, `services`, `packages`, `learning` |
| `name` | string | `null` | One collection to list the files of: a Laravel version ("12.x") or a service, package or learning source ("forge", "livewire") |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `count` | integer | yes | How many collections follow |
| `collections` | array of object | yes |  |
| `collections[].source` | string | yes | One of `core`, `services`, `packages`, `learning`. |
| `collections[].name` | string | yes | A Laravel version, or a service, package or learning source |
| `collections[].file_count` | integer | yes |  |
| `collections[].files` | array of string |  | File names ready for the read tools. Present when one collection was asked for |

### `laravel_docs_info`

Report how current this server's documentation is.

For the framework docs: the date Laravel last changed each version, and the commit this copy was taken at. For every service, package and learning source: how many pages are held, which major version they describe, and when they were last synced. Use it when a user asks how up to date the documentation is, or before telling them something newer may exist. Pass `version` to get one Laravel version only.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `version` | string | `null` | Report this Laravel version only (e.g. "12.x"). Default: every version |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `documentation_current_to` | string | yes | The date Laravel last changed any framework page in this copy, or "unknown" |
| `copy_age_days` | integer |  | Days since that date. Absent when unknown |
| `stale` | boolean |  | True when no version has changed for long enough that this copy is probably behind |
| `note` | string |  | What to do about a stale copy. Present only when stale is true |
| `default_version` | string | yes |  |
| `versions` | array of object | yes |  |
| `versions[].version` | string | yes |  |
| `versions[].available` | boolean | yes |  |
| `versions[].documentation_date` | string |  | When Laravel last changed this version's docs |
| `versions[].last_synced` | string |  |  |
| `versions[].commit` | string |  |  |
| `versions[].commit_message` | string |  |  |
| `versions[].commit_url` | string |  |  |
| `sources` | array of object | yes | Every service, package and learning source |
| `sources[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `sources[].kind` | string | yes | One of `service`, `package`, `learning`. |
| `sources[].status` | string | yes | One of `ok`, `partial`, `missing`. |
| `sources[].pages` | integer |  |  |
| `sources[].pages_expected` | integer |  |  |
| `sources[].version` | string |  | The major the source's docs are on, when it has one |
| `sources[].last_synced` | string |  | Date of the last successful sync |
| `sources[].problem` | string |  |  |

### `compare_laravel_versions`

Compare the documentation of two Laravel versions.

Lists the pages one version has and the other lacks, which is the quickest way to see what an upgrade introduces or retires. To see how a page that exists in both versions changed, read it from each with read_laravel_doc_section. `file_filter` keeps only pages whose name contains it.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `from_version` | string | required | The older version (e.g. "11.x") |  |
| `to_version` | string | required | The newer version (e.g. "12.x") |  |
| `file_filter` | string | `null` | Keep only pages whose name contains this text (e.g. "eloquent") |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `from_version` | string | yes |  |
| `to_version` | string | yes |  |
| `filter` | string |  | The file_filter that was applied, if any |
| `added_files` | array of string | yes | Pages in to_version only |
| `removed_files` | array of string | yes | Pages in from_version only |
| `common_files` | array of string | yes |  |

### `update_laravel_docs`

*Writes to the documentation directory and uses the network.*

Fetch newer documentation into this server's copy.

Needs network access and takes from seconds to a couple of minutes. scope="core" updates the framework docs for one Laravel version from GitHub. "services", "packages" and "learning" refetch those sources, all of them or the ones given in `names`. "all" does everything. Use it when laravel_docs_info shows the copy is behind and the user wants current pages; pulling a newer image or package is the other way to get them.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `scope` | string | `"core"` | What to update: "core" (default), "services", "packages", "learning" or "all" | `core`, `services`, `packages`, `learning`, `all` |
| `version` | string | `null` | Laravel version for the framework docs (e.g. "12.x"). Defaults to the server's configured version |  |
| `names` | array of string | `null` | With scope services, packages or learning: which ones (e.g. ["forge", "nova"]). Default: all of them |  |
| `force` | boolean | `false` | Refetch even if the copy is recent |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `scope` | string | yes | One of `core`, `services`, `packages`, `learning`, `all`. |
| `results` | array of object | yes |  |
| `results[].source` | string | yes | One of `core`, `services`, `packages`, `learning`. |
| `results[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `results[].outcome` | string | yes | One of `updated`, `unchanged`, `failed`. |
| `results[].commit` | string |  | For the framework docs, the commit now held |

## Package catalog and services

### `get_laravel_package`

Look up Laravel packages in the curated catalog.

With `name`: everything about one package, including what it is for, how to install it, what is typically built with it, the packages commonly used alongside it and where its documentation is. With `category`: the packages in that category. With neither: the whole catalog in brief, and the list of categories. The catalog is a hand-picked set of first-party and widely used community packages, not all of Packagist.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `name` | string | `null` | A package, by Composer name ("laravel/cashier") or short name ("cashier") |  |
| `category` | string | `null` | A category to list (e.g. "payment", "authentication") |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `count` | integer | yes |  |
| `category` | string |  | The category asked for, when one was |
| `categories` | array of string |  | Every category in the catalog. Present when the whole catalog was listed |
| `packages` | array of object | yes |  |
| `packages[].id` | string | yes | The Composer name, e.g. laravel/cashier |
| `packages[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `packages[].description` | string | yes |  |
| `packages[].categories` | array of string |  |  |
| `packages[].use_cases` | array of string |  |  |
| `packages[].installation` | string |  | The command that installs it |
| `packages[].features` | array of string |  | What is typically built with it |
| `packages[].related` | array of string |  | Ids of packages often used alongside |
| `packages[].documentation_link` | string |  | A laravel://, laravel-external:// or laravel-package:// resource URI, or a URL |
| `packages[].legacy` | boolean |  | True for a package that newer projects no longer start with |
| `packages[].superseded_by` | string |  |  |

### `recommend_laravel_packages`

Recommend packages for something the user wants to build.

Describe the need in ordinary words ("accept subscription payments", "role-based permissions", "real-time notifications") and get the catalog's best matches, best first, each with its install command and documentation link. Packages a new project would no longer start with rank below current ones. No match is a normal result with count 0.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `use_case` | string | required | What the user wants to build or solve, in plain words |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `use_case` | string | yes |  |
| `count` | integer | yes | 0 when nothing in the catalog fits |
| `packages` | array of object | yes | Best match first |
| `packages[].id` | string | yes | The Composer name, e.g. laravel/cashier |
| `packages[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `packages[].description` | string | yes |  |
| `packages[].categories` | array of string |  |  |
| `packages[].use_cases` | array of string |  |  |
| `packages[].installation` | string |  | The command that installs it |
| `packages[].features` | array of string |  | What is typically built with it |
| `packages[].related` | array of string |  | Ids of packages often used alongside |
| `packages[].documentation_link` | string |  | A laravel://, laravel-external:// or laravel-package:// resource URI, or a URL |
| `packages[].legacy` | boolean |  | True for a package that newer projects no longer start with |
| `packages[].superseded_by` | string |  |  |

### `get_laravel_service_info`

Describe one of Laravel's first-party services and what this server holds for it.

Services are Forge, Vapor, Envoyer, Nova, Cloud, Nightwatch and Herd. Returns where the service's documentation lives, how many of its pages are on this server, the major version they describe and when they were last synced. To read the pages, search with sources=["services"] or list them with list_laravel_docs.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `service` | string | required | forge, vapor, envoyer, nova, cloud, nightwatch or herd |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `id` | string | yes | Pass to list_laravel_docs as `name` to list its pages |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `documentation_url` | string | yes |  |
| `status` | string | yes | Whether this server holds its documentation One of `ok`, `partial`, `missing`. |
| `pages` | integer |  |  |
| `pages_expected` | integer |  |  |
| `version` | string |  | The major version the pages describe, when the service has one |
| `last_synced` | string |  |  |

## Learning (experimental)

### `get_laravel_learning_path`

*Experimental: may change in a minor release.*

Get a curated reading order through the Laravel documentation.

A learning path is an ordered list of framework pages for a goal such as getting started or building an API. With `path_name`, returns that path and its pages in order. Without one, lists the paths; a client that supports it is asked which the user wants.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `path_name` | string | `""` | The path's id (e.g. "getting-started"). Leave empty to list the paths |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `count` | integer | yes |  |
| `paths` | array of object | yes |  |
| `paths[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `paths[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `paths[].description` | string | yes |  |
| `paths[].difficulty` | string | yes | One of `beginner`, `intermediate`, `advanced`. |
| `paths[].estimated_hours` | number | yes |  |
| `paths[].doc_count` | integer | yes |  |
| `paths[].docs` | array of string |  | The pages to read, in order. Present when one path was asked for |
| `paths[].prerequisites` | array of string |  | Paths worth doing first |
| `paths[].services` | array of string |  | First-party services whose docs go with this path; see get_laravel_service_info |
| `paths[].packages` | array of string |  | Catalog packages that go with this path; see get_laravel_package |
| `paths[].next_path` | string |  | The path that follows this one, if any |

### `browse_docs_by_category`

*Experimental: may change in a minor release.*

Browse the framework documentation by topic or by difficulty.

With no arguments: the categories (authentication, database, testing and so on) and how many pages each holds for the selected Laravel version. With `category`, `difficulty` ("beginner", "intermediate" or "advanced") or both: the matching pages, each with its title, difficulty and categories. For a specific question, search is the better tool; this one is for seeing what exists in an area.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description | Allowed |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|---------|
| `category` | string | `null` | A topic area (e.g. "authentication", "database"). Omit both filters to list the categories |  |
| `difficulty` | string | `null` | "beginner", "intermediate" or "advanced" | `beginner`, `intermediate`, `advanced` |
| `version` | string | `null` | Laravel version (e.g. "12.x"). Defaults to the server's configured version |  |

Returns:

| Field | Type | Always | Description |
|-------|------|--------|-------------|
| `version` | string | yes |  |
| `category` | string |  |  |
| `difficulty` | string |  | One of `beginner`, `intermediate`, `advanced`. |
| `count` | integer |  | How many pages matched. Present when a filter was given |
| `docs` | array of object |  | The matching pages. Present when a filter was given |
| `docs[].file` | string | yes |  |
| `docs[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `docs[].difficulty` | string | yes |  |
| `docs[].categories` | array of string | yes |  |
| `categories` | array of object |  | Every category with its page count. Present when no filter was given |
| `categories[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `categories[].doc_count` | integer | yes |  |

## Resources

Three resource templates serve the same pages the read tools do, as markdown.

| Template | Serves |
|----------|--------|
| `laravel://{path*}` | A framework page: `laravel://queues.md`, or `laravel://12.x/queues.md` for a named version. |
| `laravel-external://{service}/{path*}` | A page of a first-party service: `laravel-external://forge/servers/php`. |
| `laravel-package://{package}/{path*}` | A page of a fetched package: `laravel-package://livewire/quickstart.md`. |
